extracted.intended_audience: contracting officers, procurement/acquisition officials, DOD/Navy implementers, policymakers and procurement analysts
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for applying OMB Circular A-76 (cost-comparison and C/I activities) including which functions may be contracted out, required exceptions, cost-comparison rules, review/notification procedures, and DOD/Navy implementation details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary reliance on private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular states that the Government should primarily rely on the private sector for goods and services; when acquiring property and services the Government shall whenever practicable rely on the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis is on effective and efficient accomplishment of Government programs rather than benefit to a particular segment of the economy. This is the foundational policy presumption to be applied unless exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inherently governmental functions must be performed in-house
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions that are inherently governmental must be performed in-house with Government personnel; a 'Government function' is one which must be performed in-house due to a special relationship in executing governmental responsibilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include discretionary application of Government authority, monitoring transactions and entitlements, and maintenance of in-house core capabilities in research and development. Such functions are excluded from contracting-out even if private sources exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue most economical performance via rigorous cost comparison
rubrics_metrics.description: When commercial performance is feasible and no overriding factors require in-house performance, the most economical performance should be pursued, including a rigorous and thorough comparison of in-house versus contractor costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost comparison is the key distinguishing element for CITA support service contracting; decisions should be driven by a thorough, equitable cost analysis rather than presumptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition of personal services contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular prohibits personal services contracts which create an employer-employee relationship between the Government and the contractor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure contracts do not substitute for civil service employment relationships; contracting vehicles that effectively replicate employment are disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No conversion based solely on personnel ceilings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular will not be used to justify conversion solely on the basis of personnel ceiling restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel ceilings cannot be the driving justification for converting in-house work to contract performance; conversions must satisfy the Circular's substantive criteria (costs, exceptions, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with laws, treaties, and international agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular will not be used when it is inconsistent with any laws, treaties, or international agreements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any A-76 implementation must respect higher-order legal obligations; do not apply Circular rules to override statutory or treaty constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preference for excess property/services from other agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property and services available from other agencies will be used in preference to new starts or conversions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before initiating new in-house starts or conversions, agencies should consider interagency resources (e.g., GSA programs) and use excess capacity when practicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three exceptions to reliance on private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: The revised Circular combines prior five exceptions into three: (1) No satisfactory commercial source is available (including delay/disruption), (2) It is in the interest of National Defense to maintain capacity within Government, (3) The Government can perform the service or provide the product at a lower cost than the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions permit justified in-house performance. Each exception has specific documentary and approval requirements (see separate entries for nonavailability and national defense).

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation required for nonavailability exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for in-house performance due to nonavailability of commercial sources requires extensive documentation of attempts to locate or develop an adequate commercial source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At minimum, announcements must be made in the Commerce Business Daily and assistance should be sought from GSA, SBA, and similar organizations. The possibility of strikes, urgency alone, or classification are not sufficient reasons by themselves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justification requirements for National Defense exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for a Government CITA on the basis of National Defense must be to satisfy training requirements or career development/rotation patterns of military personnel; personnel must be used in direct combat support roles or to maintain core capability in intermediate or depot level maintenance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such justifications must be approved at the Military Department Assistant Secretary level (e.g., ASN (MRA&L) for the Navy). The scope is limited to training/career/core-capability reasons, not general preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Common ground rules for cost comparisons (Cost Comparison Handbook)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular establishes 'common ground rules' for analyzing both Government in-house and contractor costs and mandates use of the Cost Comparison Handbook (Supplement No.1) in all instances where a cost comparison is prepared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules include: (1) use the same scope of work and level of performance for both in-house and contract analyses; (2) use the standard cost factors specified in the Handbook; (3) use full costing for Government estimates; (4) recommend pre-priced options to preclude 'buy-ins' and allow amortization of contractor startup costs; (5) obtain contract price by soliciting firm bids or proposals with the full intent to award if more cost effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar threshold and conversion/new-start differentials
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular raises the dollar limit requiring a cost comparison from $50,000 to $100,000 and establishes differentials: an existing in-house activity will not be converted to contract unless conversion results in savings of more than 10% of estimated Government personnel costs; a new start will be contracted-out unless potential savings by Government in-house performance exceed 10% of Government personnel costs plus 25% of equipment and facilities costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentials are designed to maintain status quo for existing in-house work while favoring contracting-out for new programs. No in-house activity valued over $100,000 will be converted to contract unless justified by a cost study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inventory and review schedule requirements for CITAs
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are required to compile a complete inventory of all Commercial/Industrial Type Activities (CITAs), updated annually, with greater reporting detail and a defined review schedule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must establish an initial three-year review schedule, publish it for public review, and for activities approved to remain in-house during the initial review, schedule follow-on reviews at least once every five years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set-aside programs and treatment of set-aside contracts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular specifically encourages set-aside programs to ensure small businesses (including disadvantaged firms) receive a fair portion of contracts; contracts previously awarded under set-aside programs will not be reviewed again for possible in-house performance; new requirements suitable for set-aside should be offered for contract without cost comparison.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set-aside protections mean some contracts are exempt from A-76 review. Agencies should identify set-aside-appropriate needs and offer them for contract directly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions and approvals for 'new starts' and 'expansions'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Circular provides complete definitions of 'new starts' and 'expansions' of existing in-house capabilities and requires Assistant Secretarial approval for activities that will require a large initial capital investment by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large-investment proposals must obtain higher-level approval before proceeding; clarify whether an action is a new start or expansion per the Circular's definitions before deciding contracting approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency administrative review procedures for in-house/contract decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency must establish administrative procedures to resolve questions on in-house vs contract decisions; upon written request from an affected party, the agency must have the decision reviewed by an official of the same or higher level than the official who approved the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reviewing official must assure decisions are fair, equitable, and comply with Circular guidelines. The reviewer’s decisions are final and not subject to arbitration or negotiation; the procedure covers only the decision to contract-out or perform in-house, not disputes over contractor awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost comparison process steps (Task Group, SOW, solicitations, in-house estimate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison process commences with establishment of a Task Group to prepare an acquisition schedule and develop a detailed Statement of Work (SOW); the SOW is used both to solicit contractor bids/proposals and to form the basis for the Government in-house cost estimate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Task Group responsibilities include producing the SOW, coordinating the acquisition schedule, preparing the Government estimate while solicitations are issued, and ensuring comparable scopes for fair cost comparison.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of firm bid/offer procedure and contracting officer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance (e.g., NAVMIRO, NAVSUP instructions) prescribes the use of the firm bid/offer procedure in conjunction with the cost comparison process and specifies contracting officer responsibilities for that procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting officers must solicit firm bids/offers, follow the prescribed firm bid/offer process, and understand their responsibilities in evaluating offers in light of the cost comparison results and intent to award if contract proves more cost effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAO-identified criteria for effective implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: GAO reports identified implementation deficiencies and implicitly set criteria for effective program administration: clear executive and legislative support; consistent and effective agency implementation; decisions based on strict economic basis; avoidance of personnel ceiling influence; agencies must know which programs are commercial/industrial; required reviews must be timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These GAO findings function as evaluative standards: implementation should address these weaknesses (e.g., ensure decisions are economically justified, consistent agency practices, timely reviews, clear program classification). Use GAO recommendations as performance benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to obtain contract price by soliciting firm bids/proposals with intent to award
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract price must be obtained by soliciting firm bids or proposals from the private sector with the full intent to award a contract if it is more cost effective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Solicitations must be genuine and actionable — agencies should not solicit solely to populate a cost comparison; intent to award is required to ensure competitive validity and prevent artificial underbidding.
